question: signature_leaks_internals
why: Both classes occur here for real. The positives are all the same shape — incurs types in public signatures — which is the honest answer for a CLI built on a framework, and worth measuring precisely because a reviewer stops noticing it.

items.name: build_cli
items.why: Returns incurs::cli::Cli. Changing framework, or its version, is a breaking change to this signature.

items.name: command
items.why: Returns the framework's CommandDef, so every command crate is welded to incurs' shape.

items.name: read_only
items.why: Returns McpCommandOptions, a third-party struct, as the whole of its promise.

items.name: code_for
items.why: &'static str is the contract itself — the codes are promised to callers, not an implementation detail.

items.name: add
items.why: Two integer counters. There is no internal representation to leak.

items.name: of
items.why: Takes std types and returns Self. The internals could be rewritten entirely underneath it.

items.name: lines
items.why: Returns Result<Vec<String>>: std types only, and Vec here is the promise rather than a choice of container.
